newsitem.title: UK: Marks and Spencer current sales up 8.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Marks and Spencer current sales up 8.1 pct.

text.p: Britain's biggest retailer Marks and Spencer Plc said on Wednesday sales in the 17 weeks to January 25 rose by 8.1 percent, with clothing up 9.4 percent, homeware up 33.8 percent and food up 4.6 percent.
Sales in the five weeks to January 4 were up 6.8 percent overall, with clothing up 7.2 percent, homeware 27.7 percent and foods 4.9 percent.

Marks said Christmas came late for clothing sales, but it increased its market share. Women's outerwear and men's tailoring, particularly higher-priced, more fashionable ranges, performed exceptionally well.

Better conditions in the housing market produced big sales increases in home furnishings and kitchenwear. In foods there was significant price deflation in major areas such as fruit and vegetables and peak Christmas sales came later than in previous years.

The retailer maintained margins over the 17-week period and traded at full price until after Christmas. "Over the period, costs have continued to increase at a similar level to sales, particularly where we provide specialised service" Marks said.

Overseas, total sales rose by 13.7 percent in the 17 weeks, measured in local currencies. Sales in Europe, excluding Britain, rose by 24.4 percent and in the Far East by 18.1 percent. Sales at Brooks Brothers in the United States rose by 9.6 percent and Kings supermarkets were up 1.5 percent. -- London Newsroom 44-171-542-7717
